title: Indian Passport Now Offers Visa-Free or Visa-on-Arrival Access to 74 Countries
excerpt: India's Ministry of External Affairs lists 27 visa-free and 47 visa-on-arrival destinations for Indian citizens in 2026, with Malaysia, Thailand, and Kazakhstan among the notable entries.
body:
• Indian passport holders can now enter 27 countries without a visa and 47 more with visa-on-arrival, according to the Ministry of External Affairs.
  • Malaysia extended visa-free access for Indians through December 2026, while Thailand, Kazakhstan, and several Caribbean nations remain on the visa-free list.
  • Spain, France, and Germany eliminated transit visa requirements for Indians transiting to non-EU destinations in 2026, easing European stopovers.
  • Argentina now allows visa-free entry for Indians holding valid U.S. B2, J, H-1B, or other select visas, or a U.S. Green Card.

Expanding Access for Indian Travelers

Indian passport holders now enjoy visa-free or visa-on-arrival access to 74 countries and territories worldwide, a steady expansion from what was available a decade ago, according to the latest data from India's Ministry of External Affairs. The figure includes 27 destinations that require no visa at all and 47 that issue visas upon arrival at the port of entry.

The updated list, corroborated by the Henley Passport Index 2026 and travel advisory platforms, reflects a combination of bilateral agreements, tourism-driven policy changes, and India's growing diplomatic engagement across Asia, Africa, and the Caribbean.

Where Indians Can Travel Visa-Free

The 27 visa-free destinations span multiple continents. In Asia, Bhutan, Kazakhstan, Macao, Malaysia, Nepal, and Thailand allow Indian nationals to enter without advance visa processing. Malaysia's visa-free window, extended through December 31, 2026, requires travelers to complete a Malaysia Digital Arrival Card (MDAC) before departure.

In the Caribbean, Barbados, Dominica, Grenada, Haiti, Jamaica, Montserrat, St. Vincent and the Grenadines, and Trinidad and Tobago welcome Indian travelers without visas. African destinations include Angola, Mauritius, Rwanda, and Senegal, while Pacific island nations such as Fiji, Cook Islands, Micronesia, Niue, and Vanuatu round out the list.

"Indian citizens have access to 27 visa-free, 47 visa-on-arrival and 66 e-visa countries as of 2026."

— Ministry of External Affairs, Government of India

Visa-on-Arrival Options

The 47 visa-on-arrival destinations include several popular travel corridors. Indonesia, Cambodia, Laos, Sri Lanka, and the Maldives in Asia all process visas at arrival. In Africa, Ethiopia, Tanzania, Madagascar, Mozambique, Seychelles, and Zimbabwe offer on-arrival processing. Jordan and Qatar provide the same in the Middle East.

The process varies by country but generally requires a valid passport, return ticket, proof of accommodation, and sufficient funds. Processing times at immigration counters typically range from 15 minutes to an hour.

New Developments in 2026

Several policy changes this year have expanded options for Indian travelers. Argentina opened visa-free entry effective April 2026 for Indians holding a valid U.S. visa of type B2, J, B1, O, P, E, or H-1B, or a U.S. Green Card. The policy directly benefits the roughly 4.5 million Indian-origin residents of the United States who hold these documents.

Three major European nations also eased transit rules. Spain removed its transit visa requirement for Indians transiting to non-EU countries on March 4, France followed on April 10, and Germany did the same on June 3. While these changes do not grant entry to Schengen countries, they significantly simplify connections through Madrid, Paris, and Frankfurt—three of Europe's busiest transit hubs.

On the restrictive side, Nicaragua eliminated its visa-on-arrival program in February 2026, moving Indian citizens to a category requiring advance visa processing.

What This Means for the Diaspora

For the estimated 32 million-strong Indian diaspora, the expanding visa-free list creates new leisure and business travel corridors. Indians holding U.S., UK, or Schengen visas or residency already benefit from additional access—countries like South Korea, Mexico, Colombia, Georgia, and Serbia waive visa requirements for Indian nationals with valid visas from these blocs.

Travel industry platforms recommend that diaspora travelers verify requirements directly with destination embassies before booking, as policies can change with little notice. The Ministry of External Affairs maintains an updated list on its official website.

Beyond Visa-Free: The E-Visa Expansion

In addition to the 74 visa-free and visa-on-arrival destinations, 66 countries now offer Indian citizens electronic visa processing, which eliminates the need for in-person consular visits. Combined, Indian passport holders can access over 140 destinations with relatively streamlined entry procedures—a marked improvement from the sub-60 figure of a decade ago, though still well below the 190-plus destinations accessible to holders of the strongest passports.
